doc.title: Anat Cohen interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2021

title: What she hopes audiences hear: emotional impact and meaning
summary: Notes are a tool; she wants music to have emotional impact and be meaningful to her and the audience.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Playing for the audience: communicating from the bandstand

blocks.x: Do you have hopes for what your audience is absorbing from your music? There’s things that happen onstage that you and musicians in general think oh that was a wonderful moment. Or if you write a melody, I’m trying to form this question about what do you think your audience is hearing in contrast to what you’re hearing?

I would love to interview the audience. I don’t know in contrast to what I’m hearing. I don’t know what — I don’t know how they perceive the music but I know that ultimately the notes, they’re just a tool you know, the goal is to create an emotional impact, to let people — I can’t say forget about their lives for a moment because you know music like

scent, like smell, it brings you back to moments in your life easily. Like you will hear a song that you heard when you were a kid and you’re like oh my God, I just remembered this moment. Or you smell something from the garden of your neighbors that you’re like I know this smell and it brings you back to a moment. So I don’t know if music can always let people forget about their lives or remind them of things they try to forget or wanted to remember, but I do want my music to have an emotional impact and I want it to be meaningful. Also for me. I mean I’m a little bit selfish here, because you know I don’t want to go to the other side of the world and you know, do three Covid tests and travel and you know go take a few flights and then to arrive to a place and just play notes. That’s not enough for me. I want to get off stage and to know that it was meaningful to me, that I connected with the other musicians and by that hoping to be connected to the audience and to take them with me on a little journey, away from their moment. So that’s all.
